title: Expose rule-awareness relationships and positive capability bindings in-band
description:
Put runtime-useful rule-awareness metadata in pack/runtime-owned data: stable
identities, provenance-linked relationships and aliases, known ambiguity/adjudication
information, and positively selected deterministic capability bindings with explicit
limits. Do not create a uniform execution-readiness disposition for every clause.
A missing capability binding means only that Eshyra has not positively selected that
deterministic operation.
design:
Stabilize the capability-ID vocabulary jointly with E0 — A4 emits the requirement,
E0 owns the ledger and the exact membership. Reuse the existing magic-item
engineHooks shape ({engine, hook}) as the starting point since it is already
proven over 1,016 clauses, but do not inherit its gaps: hook entries currently
carry no per-hook implementation status.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime consumers can obtain stable identities, provenance, useful relationships, known ambiguity, and positive capability availability/limits without reading audit-only reports.
- A capability binding names a concrete bounded operation/identity/revision and its exclusions or residual DM interpretation.
- Absence of capability/readiness metadata never means a rule has no mechanic, is irrelevant, or is safely unsupported.
- Model-adjudicated material does not require exhaustive per-clause exception labeling.
- Unknown/unclassified values cannot become a green readiness result.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.
GREEN DEFINITION — shared verbatim by 19.1.4, 19.1.5, 19.4.5 and 19.5.12. A
clause is green ONLY when all eight hold:
  1. The complete source clause has been identified.
  2. Every deterministic branch is projected.
  3. All source and derived fields are provenanced.
  4. Every required capability is identified.
  5. The engine implementation exists.
  6. An executable conformance scenario proves the intended outcome.
  7. Runtime lookup can find the canonical clause.
  8. Unsupported portions fail closed.
A representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green. The Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but explicitly
did NOT prove the semantic appropriateness of every free-form effect.

COUNT HYGIENE: every number in this bead is a SNAPSHOT at commit 4384f25. The
generated ledger/predicate is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a
hand-copied number (e.g. 391, 399, 77, 79).
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.
ADR-0020 authority reconciliation applied 2026-09-10 by eshyra-o9bd.19.6.5.
The operative title/description/acceptance criteria supersede contradictory
pre-ADR global-closure language in older notes. Historical notes remain evidence,
not current authority.
=== DESIGN SESSION 2026-09-12 (Claude Captain; design-only, no code yet) ===
Authority: ADR 0020 (esp. SS1, SS3, SS4, SS8 restraint), docs/design/evidence-trust-model.md
(F4, eshyra-o9bd.19.1.16), W13 capability-contract shape (eshyra-olc5.6, CLOSED - this bead

--- WHAT IS ALREADY IN-BAND (confirm with assertions; do NOT rebuild) ---
* stable identity      -> RulesRecord.key
* provenance           -> RulesRecord.provenance {sourceRef, locator} + field-provenance.json
                          (packages/core/src/rules/fieldProvenance.ts, per (kind, pointerPrefix))
* known ambiguity      -> data.mechanics.ambiguities; 3 entries in the shipped pack
                          (magic-item:cube-of-force, spell:create-undead, spell:find-familiar);
                          already read in-band by discovery/packet.ts::ambiguities.
The residual defect is exactly two things: RELATIONSHIPS and CAPABILITY BINDINGS.

--- ROOT CAUSE 1: relationships are a hardcoded CONSUMER-side allowlist ---
packages/core/src/discovery/expansion.ts::directLinks hardcodes the traversable field set
(data.source, data.parentClass, data.progressionTableRef, tableRefs, spellTableRefs,
statBlockRefs, mechanics.conditions[].condition) AND the per-field target-resolution mode.
Field NAME does not determine meaning. Measured over the shipped pack (1812 records):
    feature.source              n=184  resolved=184   (a real record key, 'class:barbarian')
    ancestry.source             n=13   resolved=0     (the literal label "race" - a source
                                                       SECTION, not a record key)
    subclass.parentClass        12/12   class.progressionTableRef 12/12
    rule.tableRefs 38/38  magic-item.tableRefs 32/32  magic-item.statBlockRefs 2/2
    spell.tableRefs 9/9   feature.tableRefs 4/4  background.tableRefs 4/4
    subclass.spellTableRefs 10/10      mechanics.conditions 195 refs, 0 unresolved
The importer ALREADY KNOWS the distinction and writes it down - in
scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts REASON PROSE:
  ancestry '/source' = "a structural field describing where this ancestry sits in the
                        source (page/section), not narrative prose."
  feature  '/source' = "the granting class/subclass record-key, not source text."
No consumer can act on prose. So expansion applies one meaning to both kinds and silently
drops all 13 ancestry links: directLinks' add() returns early when the key does not resolve.
"not a reference", "target pack absent" and "expansion found nothing" are indistinguishable
- recurring idiom 1 of eshyra-o9bd.19.7 / ADR 0020 SS3.
This is the SAME defect class fieldProvenance.ts was built to close (one JS string field,
two meanings, consumer guessing from shape), and it takes the same shape of fix.

--- ROOT CAUSE 2: the capability ledger is AUDIT-ONLY ---
The only reviewed statement of Eshyra's positively selected deterministic capabilities and
their bindings to record identities lives in an AUDIT-BUNDLE SCRIPT:
  packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS  (resolve-check-v1, resolve-concentration-v1,
                                              resolve-spell-upcast-v1)
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_BINDINGS   (8 rule keys -> capability, many-to-many)
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_DISPOSITIONS (31 explicit not-positively-selected rows)
No runtime consumer may import it. So discovery/packet.ts::capabilities() instead hardcodes
`record.kind !== 'magic-item'` plus a direct import of ONE contract constant
(MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY), and every other declaration arrives from a TEST
FIXTURE table (test/discovery/support/scenario.ts DECLARED_OFFLINE_CAPABILITIES).
Consequence, verified against the pack: all 8 W13-bound rule records exist
(rule:ability-checks, rule:advantage-and-disadvantage, rule:attack-rolls,
rule:modifiers-to-the-roll, rule:proficiency-bonus, rule:saving-throws, rule:concentration,
rule:casting-a-spell-at-a-higher-level) and every one of them reaches the DM context packet
with ZERO capability entries - byte-identical to a record for which nothing was positively
selected. That directly violates this bead's 3rd acceptance criterion.
packetMessage.ts already renders the non-claim correctly ("no capability was positively
selected. / This is not a claim that the record has no mechanics..."). The renderer is
honest; the DATA is missing.

--- REQUIRED INVARIANT ---
Every rule-awareness fact a runtime consumer needs - stable identity, provenance, declared
relationships, known ambiguity, and positively selected capability bindings with their
limits - is obtainable from pack- or runtime-owned data reachable from @eshyra/core, and
every negative result is a distinguishable typed disposition, never an empty value or a
silent drop.

--- OWNERSHIP SPLIT (this bead owns MECHANISM, not membership) ---
* eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4 (this bead): the in-band representation + runtime access contract +
  fail-closed semantics, seeded with the already-reviewed content that exists today.
* eshyra-o9bd.19.2.4: pack-side CONTENT - canonical identities, aliases, topics, the
  populated many-to-many relationship set. (38 duplicate (kind, normalized-name) groups
  exist in the shipped pack; aliases are 19.2.4's content job, not this bead's.)
* eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12: the authoritative LEDGER MEMBERSHIP of selected capabilities.
* eshyra-olc5.6 (W13, CLOSED): the capability CONTRACT SHAPE. Not re-owned here.
Asymmetry, and it is principled: relationship meaning is PACK-specific (an add-on's fields
differ) so it is a PACK artifact; capability selection is ESHYRA-specific so it is a
RUNTIME module. That is what "pack/runtime-owned data" in the description means.

--- DELIVERABLE 1: pack-owned record-relationship manifest ---
New packages/core/src/rules/recordRelationships.ts, mirroring fieldProvenance.ts exactly
(same house style, same (kind, pointerPrefix) declaration model with array indices collapsed
to '*', same longest-prefix-wins matching, same no-silent-default rule).
  RecordRelationshipDeclaration {kind, pointerPrefix, disposition, relation?,
                                 targetResolution?, targetKind?, reason}
  disposition: 'reference' | 'not-a-reference'   <- ancestry '/source' is declared
    not-a-reference WITH its reason, so "declared not to be a link" is distinguishable from
    "nobody classified it".
  targetResolution: 'record-key' | 'record-name' (record-name requires targetKind; that is
    the mechanics.conditions case, resolved through normalizeRulesRecordName).
  Resolution returns a DISCRIMINATED UNION per value, never a filtered array:
    {outcome:'resolved', targetRecordKey, ...}
    {outcome:'unresolved-target', rawValue, reason:'no-record-with-key'|'no-record-with-name'
                                  |'ambiguous-name', ...}
  An unresolved target is RETAINED and reported, never dropped. That closes the fail-open.
  Fail-closed gate (bounded population, independently justified - it comes from the DELETED
  consumer allowlist, not from the pack under repair): every (kind, pointerPrefix) the old
  expansion.ts allowlist recognized must have an explicit declaration, and every declaration
  must match at least one real leaf pointer in the emitted pack (dead-declaration check).
  NO corpus-wide coverage gate over RulesRecord.data - ADR 0020 forbids the global negative.
  Emitted as record-relationships.json beside field-provenance.json from a curated compiler
  input scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/recordRelationshipDeclarations.ts (ADR 0017 SS3
  curated input, not a hand-edit of output); loaded by packLoader.ts
  loadRecordRelationshipManifest; surfaced by bundledSrdPack.ts; threaded into
  expandTypedRelationships by harness.ts exactly as the field-provenance manifest already is.
  discovery/expansion.ts::directLinks is DELETED and replaced by manifest-driven resolution -
  the same consumer-heuristic deletion PR #543 performed on PROJECTION_CONTAINER_KEYS.
  A pack with no manifest declares no relationships and SAYS SO (explicit manifest-absent
  note); it must NOT fall back to the old allowlist.

--- DELIVERABLE 2: runtime-owned deterministic capability ledger ---
New packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts. MOVE (not copy) the three W13
contracts, the 8 bindings and the 31 not-positively-selected dispositions out of the audit
bundle into src/rules/; the audit bundle then IMPORTS them, reversing the dependency and
keeping its reporting intact. Keep the runtime-owner fields (inputSchemaOperation,
runtimeOwner, evidence) - they are real capability-owner facts.
  Lookup is a discriminated union, never a bare array:
    {outcome:'bound', bindings}                       - contracts quoted, not restated
    {outcome:'not-positively-selected', disposition}  - the 31 explicit rows
    {outcome:'no-statement'}                          - the ledger makes NO statement about
                                                        this record. NOT absence of mechanics.
  requireCapabilityContract(revision) THROWS on an unknown revision (fail closed).
  discovery/packet.ts::capabilities consults the ledger by record key instead of the
  `kind === 'magic-item'` branch. A bound rule record gets a 'not-evaluated-offline'
  CapabilityPreflight quoting the contract's identity/revision/inputs/exclusions/residual -
  which is EXACTLY what the F4 evidence model permits for a declaration without the owner's
  subject-specific preflight ("a capability declaration qualifies its identity/revision and
  its declared inputs, exclusions and residual interpretation; it does NOT qualify
  availability"). The magic-item real preflight path is unchanged. No capability is inferred
  from typed-field presence (W13 prohibition preserved).

--- REGRESSION PREDICATE (assert identities, never counts - idiom 3) ---
R1 ancestry:dwarf '/source' resolves to a declared not-a-reference disposition carrying its
   reason; it produces no traversal AND no silent drop. feature:barbarian:ability-score-
   improvement '/source' resolves to class:barbarian as a 'granted-by' reference. Both from
   the SAME field name - the discriminating control the old code fails.
R2 A declaration naming a pointer no record emits fails the build (dead declaration).
R3 A reference value naming an absent key yields {outcome:'unresolved-target'} and appears in
   the trace; it is never filtered out.
R4 Each of the 8 W13-bound rule keys, by identity, yields {outcome:'bound'} with the exact
   expected capability revision, and reaches a context packet with a declared capability
   entry. rule:attunement (a disposition row) yields 'not-positively-selected' with its
   reason. A record in neither list yields 'no-statement'.
R5 requireCapabilityContract('not-a-real-revision') throws; an unknown binding revision fails
   the ledger's own validation at construction.
R6 No capability entry is produced for any record merely because it carries typed mechanics.
R7 The audit bundle's reported rows remain identical after the move (same identities).

--- PROHIBITIONS ---
No uniform execution-readiness disposition for every clause. No corpus-wide capability or
relationship inventory and no completeness claim. No coverage gate over RulesRecord.data. No
alias/topic CONTENT (that is 19.2.4). No change to the W13 contract shape (olc5.6). No new
proof system beside the existing readiness machinery (ADR 0017 SS8 / ADR 0020 restraint).
Absence of a binding is a statement about Eshyra, never about the rules.

--- BLOCKING, BOTH CHILDREN ---
B1 NO REGRESSION COVERAGE AT ALL. Every predicate in both specs is missing: z7bm R1-R6 and
   xus8 R1-R7. The two discriminating controls that ARE the deliverable are absent:
     * z7bm R1 - ancestry:dwarf vs feature:barbarian:ability-score-improvement, same
       '/source' field name, opposite dispositions. This is the entire point of the bead.
     * xus8 R3 - a context packet containing rule:concentration carrying a declared
       capability entry naming resolve-concentration-v1. This must FAIL against pre-fix
       behaviour; nothing demonstrates that it does.
   In this program the regression predicate IS the deliverable. A mechanism with no
   discriminating test is precisely the "machinery that looks green because it recognises
   nothing" that invalidated PRs #475/#476/#477 (eshyra-o9bd.19.7, recurring idiom 1) and
   that ADR 0020 section 3 forbids. Neither branch may merge.

--- BLOCKING, eshyra-xus8 ---
X1 DUPLICATED THE LEDGER INSTEAD OF MOVING IT. The spec said, capitalised, "MOVE - do not
   copy". The audit bundle's RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS (3),

X2 LAYER INVERSION, UNDECLARED. src/rules/ now imports ../model/toolSchemaValidation.js,
   ../orchestrator/tools.js and ../state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts. rules/ was a near-leaf
   layer; it now depends on the orchestrator tool registry. state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts
   already imports rules/deterministicCapabilityContract.js, so rules -> state -> rules.
   No hard cycle today, but the spec explicitly asked the child to state which direction it
   chose and why, and the notes are silent. The duplicated ruleCapabilityInputCheck helper

X3 Throws bare `Error`, not a named class extending RulesPackError. fieldProvenance.ts and
   the sibling child's recordRelationships.ts both follow the RulesPackError convention.

--- BLOCKING, eshyra-z7bm ---
Z1 THE MANIFEST IS AN OPTIONAL OPTION THAT SILENTLY DEFAULTS TO "NO RELATIONSHIPS".
   expandTypedRelationships(candidates, stack) with options.relationshipManifest omitted
   returns zero traversals. Any call site not updated degrades silently and the compiler
   cannot catch it, because the field is optional. That is the fail-open idiom restated:
   a missing input produces an empty successful result. Make it a required parameter so
   omission is a type error.
Z2 traversalOf RECONSTRUCTS linkField FROM THE POINTER WITH A STRING HACK, including a
   hardcoded special case `pointer === '/mechanics/conditions/*/condition' ?
   'data.mechanics.conditions' : ...replaceAll('/', '.')`. This reintroduces exactly the
   consumer-side string heuristic the bead exists to DELETE, and it is load-bearing: route
   triggers are `${linkField}:${relation}`, so dedup and route identity now depend on it.
   The declaration must carry the linkField (or TypedTraversal must carry the declaration
   identity); it must not be re-derived.
Z3 CONDITION RELATION IS RESOLVED BY NAME, NOT BY ENTRY. conditionRelation() returns the
   relation of the FIRST mechanics.conditions entry whose condition matches, because
   walkFieldPointers collapses the array index to '*' and the real index is lost. If one
   record ever lists the same condition twice with different relations, every occurrence
   takes the first entry's relation. The OLD code was structurally immune - it iterated
   entries and read each entry's own relation. I checked the shipped pack: 0 records
   currently exhibit this, so it is latent, not active. That is exactly the kind of
   accidentally-green mechanism this program must stop shipping. Resolve per entry.
Z4 'relationship-manifest-absent' IS PUSHED AS A CANDIDATE LOSS. A missing manifest is a
   configuration fact, not a candidate the stage lost. losses feed measurements.ts:492
   perStage.losses counts, and design section 13.3 gives a stage's loss accounting a
   specific meaning. Carry it as its own trace field.
Z5 UNRESOLVED-TARGET IS DEAD CODE WITH NO EVIDENCE. After ancestry '/source' is correctly
   declared not-a-reference, the shipped pack has ZERO unresolved targets, so the entire
   unresolved path never executes in any run. Combined with B1 it is unexercised in every
   sense. Its detail field also uses a double cast (`resolution as unknown as
   Record<string, unknown>`).

xus8: the ledger module's content and shape, the discriminated CapabilityLedgerLookup with
